claims.wording: The TSC2026 abstract reports an excess of above-chance receivers in 100 screened Mind-to-Mind dyads relative to a binomial null model.
claims.outcome_definition: Reported count of receivers meeting a task-performance criterion versus a binomial expectation; not an overall hit rate and not 100 successful pairs.
supporting_observations: The conference entry reports a positive result without numerical test details.
competing_explanations: A reproducible task effect is a candidate interpretation; the abstract does not identify its cause.
Selection, dependence, criterion choice or ordinary information leakage require evaluation; none is established here.
missing_evidence: Successful-receiver count, per-receiver trials, null success probability, threshold, test direction, exact p-value and uncertainty are absent from the inspected abstract.
Complete protocol, preregistration, randomization/blinding logs, exclusions, multiplicity handling and attrition are needed.
No participant-level Mind2Mind dataset or executable analysis was obtained. Independent replication and a systematic contrary-evidence search are pending.
Independent human source verification and methodological review remain pending.

claims.wording: The telephone-study abstract reports 50.0% accuracy over 210 pre-selected completer trials against 33.3% chance, p<.001.
claims.outcome_definition: Correct caller guesses among pre-selected completer trials; 210 is a trial count, not a participant count.
supporting_observations: Author-reported accuracy and significance; no recalculated test.
counter_evidence: The same paper reports a nonsignificant post-selected condition; it is a different timing condition, not a direct replication.
competing_explanations: Authors discuss a psi interpretation; statistical significance alone does not establish telepathy.
Conventional cues, protocol amendments, selection and repeated observations are alternative concerns requiring methods/data review.
missing_evidence: Full-text copies, preprint supplementary output and KPU1062 revisions are now inspected by AI. Independent methodological review of protocol changes, dependence, selection and null-model choice remains pending.

claims.wording: The same abstract reports 31.9% accuracy over 630 post-selected completer trials against 33.3% chance, p=.61.
claims.outcome_definition: Correct guesses when caller selection followed the guess; distinct from pre-selection.
supporting_observations: Author-reported nonsignificant outcome; no recalculated test.
counter_evidence: Pre-selected trials in the same study were reported above chance; the conditions cannot be pooled as one endpoint.
competing_explanations: Results are compatible with chance under the reported analysis.
A small or heterogeneous effect could remain undetected; nonsignificance is not proof of no effect.

claims.wording: The survey abstract reports that 93.2% of 175 scientist/engineer respondents endorsed at least one exceptional experience.
claims.outcome_definition: Self-report endorsement of any of 25 categories, not telepathy-specific prevalence or experimental performance.
supporting_observations: Reported respondent-group proportion; no item-level verification.
competing_explanations: Reports can be meaningful lived experiences without verifying an anomalous mechanism.
Recall, interpretation and nonresponse selection may affect endorsement; these explanations were not tested here.
missing_evidence: Full questionnaire, response-rate details, weighting and item-level tables need inspection.
The inspected abstract does not establish the telepathy-specific 70% figure on the IONS overview; it is not promoted into this record.
Independent human source verification and methodological review remain pending.
